s01_hook.text: At first glance, this trajectory looks successful.
PlanT-2 earns a perfect driving score and avoids every collision.
s01_hook.tts: Plan T Two earns a perfect driving score and avoids every collision.

s01_hook.text: Now watch the rule itself. At step fifty, the car keeps moving.
It fails to yield at the crosswalk. High metrics have hidden an illegal behavior.

s02_benchmark.tts: Traffic Sign Bench makes rule compliance verifiable.

s02_benchmark.text: Thirty-four signs, automatic checkers, and twenty-nine thousand targeted scenarios.

s02b_taxonomy.text: We start from all eight Vienna Convention classes.
We retain only signs that impose explicit obligations with verifiable rule logic.
Thirty-four signs remain, grouped by what capability they demand of the ego vehicle: priority, speed, obstacles, and routing.

s07_portability.text: Across countries, rule meaning overlaps by ninety-two percent.
Change the appearance; reuse the same checker.

s03_realmaps.text: Every test begins with real road geometry: twenty-six thousand Moscow road fragments.
We preserve three structural families: junctions, dual-path maps, and corridors.
A sign turns each fragment into a simulator scene—and an executable closed-loop rule test.

s16_diversity.text: For each map, we sample ten controlled closed-loop variants.
We vary spawn lane, route, speed, traffic density, and background dynamics.
Ten variants per map yield twenty-nine thousand scenarios—and robust evaluation.

s09_gap.text: We next evaluate standard planners. The metric is SCD: obey the sign and reach the destination.
s09_gap.tts: We next evaluate standard planners. The metric is S C D: obey the sign and reach the destination.

s09_gap.text: Standard planners score only two point nine to nine percent.

s10_architecture.text: To close the gap, PlanT-2 learns from privileged, rule-compliant experts.
s10_architecture.tts: To close the gap, Plan T Two learns from privileged, rule-compliant experts.

s10_architecture.text: Eight experts drive each scenario. Failed rollouts are discarded.
We retain the top two successful trajectories by speed and comfort: thirty-six thousand eight hundred twenty-eight high-quality examples.
Each frame becomes input: objects, sign, route, and local map.
Persistent sign-state and learned speed tokens carry the active rule and vehicle speed.
We train on expert path, waypoints, and speed, adding just zero point four percent new parameters.
On held-out tests, overall SCD rises from five point nine to seventy-two point three percent, with gains in every group.
s10_architecture.tts: On held-out tests, overall S C D rises from five point nine to seventy-two point three percent, with gains in every group.

s15_conclusion.text: Therefore, this work shows that traffic-rule compliance must be tested explicitly.
TrafficSignBench does it at scale: thirty-four signs, twenty-nine thousand closed-loop scenarios.
s15_conclusion.tts: Traffic Sign Bench does it at scale: thirty-four signs, twenty-nine thousand closed-loop scenarios.

s15_conclusion.text: Safe autonomous driving needs scores that catch rule compliance—not only the destination or comfort.
